# Friendly Neighborhood Status Indicator

[![Platform: Squeak](https://img.shields.io/badge/Squeak-F8F8F8?logo=data:image/svg%2bxml;base64,)](https://squeak.org/)
[![Language: Smalltalk-80](https://img.shields.io/badge/Smalltalk--80-B8DAFD)](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Smalltalk)
[![License: MIT](https://img.shields.io/badge/License-MIT-yellow)](LICENSE)

An archived Squeak/Smalltalk project that combined real-time procedural flame graphics with a desktop availability display running on a dedicated Raspberry Pi device for open-office environments, in a fun and highly visible way.

The system ran on a Raspberry Pi and provided a visual indication of whether I was Available or Busy, while also serving as an experiment in generating animated graphics in real-time using Smalltalk.

`FlamesRefactor.st` contains the complete implementation written in Smalltalk-80 for the Squeak platform. [Squeak](https://squeak.org/) is a _dialect_ of the [Smalltalk-80 programming language](https://wiki.squeak.org/squeak/373).

## Problem

In an open office environment, there was no simple equivalent of a closed office door for signaling "please do not disturb."

The goals were:

- Provide coworkers with an easy visual indication of availability
- Experiment with procedural graphics and animation
- Build a graphical application for Raspberry Pi without needing traditional Linux GUI frameworks

Squeak provided a platform that solved all three problems simultaneously.

## Project History

This project began in March 2020 using Squeak 5.3. Using a Raspberry Pi and touchscreen, I built a desktop availability display around my Smalltalk port of FireDemo, capable of showing different animated graphics to indicate whether I was Available or Busy.

The project remained under active development for roughly two years. During that time I explored both procedural graphics and UI development in Smalltalk while learning the Raspberry Pi platform.

Eventually I figured out how to run my C# applications on Linux, allowing me to return to the faster and more familiar implementation path. The project was subsequently ported back to C# and development continued there.

This repository is preserved as an example of exploratory programming in Smalltalk-80 and is **not under active development**. It may require modifications to work with current Squeak versions.

### Alternate Names for this project

- NDADD — Neighborhood Desktop Availability Display Device (V1)
- NDDADD Mark II — Neighborhood Display Device for Availability & Delightful Distractions (V2)
- FNSI — Friendly Neighborhood Status Indicator (V3)
  - This name stuck after adding a flaming Batman logo. "Friendly Neighborhood..." felt _vaguely_ superhero-themed, so I stopped trying to rename the project every release.
- Other ideas:
  - ASID — Availability Status Indicator and Deflector
  - FANSI DAD — Friendly Amusing Neighborhood Status Indicator Display for Availability and Deflection
  - PASIDINA — Personal Availability Status Information Desktop Indicator in the Neighborhood Assistant
  - SIPI CUP: Status Indicator for Presence Information ...(it) can update people? ...and Conversational Obstruction Plan
  - MAGPAI — My Automated Great Personal Availability Indicator
  - ABSURD — Automated Busy Status and Ultra Randomization Deflector
  - NORAD — Neighborhood Obstructor of Randomization and Automated Deflection

## Related Projects

### Predecessor & Successor Project

[`FireDemo`](https://github.com/redgreenshift/firedemo) occupies the unusual position of being both the direct predecessor and the direct successor of this project.

`Friendly Neighborhood Status Indicator` began as a specialized application built on top of the original `FireDemo` flame effects. Later, the lessons learned here were folded back into `FireDemo` and then the graphics engine was expanded with additional effects such as lightning, plasma, and more.

See the [`FireDemo` Project History](https://github.com/redgreenshift/FireDemo/blob/main/README.md#funny-circular-lineage) for the full explanation of this somewhat circular lineage.
